## rnorm Function

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
rnorm(10)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
rnorm(10)>1
sum(rnorm(10)>1) #returns the buber which are greater than 1
sum(rnorm(10)>1)/10 #gives the proportion of random numbers greater than 1
mean(rnorm(10)>1) #Same thing
1-pnorm(1) #exactl prob
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}

vectex
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
vectex[7]
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
listex = list(c(T,F,T), 1:5, 6)
listex[2]
#unlist(listex[2,3]) #unlist funciton will take the two and three list compoents and force them into one, it will create a new numeric vector of length 6
unlist(listex) #creates numeric vector (double) of length 9 via coercion
```
## Exercise
```{r, echo=FALSE}
x = rnorm(100)
y = rnorm(100)
holdlmout = lm(y~x) # linear regression of y on x
#now holdmout is a list consisting of the important results of linear regression
attributes(holdlmout) #attributes and names gives a list of components of the objects
names(holdlmout)
holdlmout$coefficients
```
## Attributes
```{r, echo=FALSE}
as.integer(factor(c(0,1,2))) # Coercion from factor to integer, looks at that position that level is in the list of levels -- 0 is the first level, 1 is the second level, 2 is the third level. So when coerced back into integers, displays "1 2 3"
```
## Matrices
```{r, echo=FALSE}
matex = matrix(1:6, nrow=2)
print(matex)
c(nrow(matex),ncol(matex))
rbind(1:3,4:6,7:9) # bind by row
cbind(cbind(1:3,4:6,7:9), rbind(1:3,4:6,7:9)) #bind by colmun
```
## Rep
```{r, echo=FALSE}
n=3
m=3
rep(1:n,m)
matrix(rep(1:n,m),nrow=n)
```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
gradebook = data.frame(
Name = c("Miguel","Yotam","Mary","Jing"),
HWScore = c(98, 87, 99, 78),
ExamScore = c(92, 91, 87, 95),
FinalGrade = c("A", "A-", "A", "B"),
stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

gradebook
gradebook$Name
factor(gradebook$FinalGrade)
gradebook$FinalGrade
```
